answer: One defense is a bonded identity: each agent locks a stake behind its name, like an opal set in a ring, before it can earn anything. Peers who later catch two identities colluding or voting in lockstep can prove it and trigger a slash of both bonds. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake across a canyon of locked capital, while the nectar of rewards flows only to accounts that survive scrutiny over many epochs. Each extra puppet multiplies the capital at risk, so cloning identities costs more than it returns.
